Why distill? A 14B model with web search is slow (tens of seconds per answer), needs a GPU and the internet, and costs money per query. For a narrow domain you can move that knowledge into a model 100× smaller that answers in a second on a phone, with no server at all.

Sequence-level distillation. The student never sees the wiki. It only sees what the teacher wrote, so everything it knows came through the teacher. Ollama returns text, not probabilities, so this is the same "learn from the teacher's answers" recipe used to make most small open models. Part two shows what changes when an API also leaks probabilities.

Why the student can beat the teacher. Without search, qwen3:14b half-remembers the show from pre-training and confidently invents details ("the car wash is called Lucky 7"). The student was trained only on the teacher's grounded answers, so on this narrow topic it is more accurate than the teacher's own memory. Outside the topic it knows nothing, by design.

Honest numbers. The 100 fan questions were written by hand before training and checked against the wiki. Held-out rephrasings are wordings of trained facts that were removed from training. Answers are graded by keyword for the fan set and by the teacher (with the wiki answer as reference) for the rest. Everything ({pages} pages, {facts} facts, {rows} rows) was produced on one Windows PC with an RTX 4070 Ti; code is on GitHub.
